### Investment Memo: AS (Amer Sports, Inc.) — 18 November 2026

**Verdict**: HOLD | Conviction: Medium
**Price Target**: $34 (~12% upside from current $30.24)
**Time Horizon**: 12–24 months

---

**Investment Thesis**

Amer Sports is a genuinely high-quality compounder — 25–26% guided FY26 growth, ~1,000bps of five-year gross-margin expansion, a transformed balance sheet (net leverage 0.31x, BBB−), clean earnings (Beneish −2.46, 171% cash conversion), and a fresh $1bn buyback — trading at 22.7x forward / 18.4x FY27E earnings, roughly a PEG of 1.0. The problem is that this quality is already approximately priced: our value work puts fair value at ~$31, the macro regime (10Y at 5.13%, USD +4% in eight weeks, record-low sentiment) is compressing exactly the kind of high-beta, long-duration multiple AS carries, and the growth engine is dangerously concentrated — ~85–90% of incremental revenue is coming from China/APAC under a Chinese controlling shareholder, in a boycott-prone market, with tariff-refund-flattered 2026 margins and zero insider buying in twelve months. This is a good company at a fair price with a fat left tail: hold, add on weakness, respect the triggers.

---

**Key Findings by Domain**

- **Macro & Sector**: AS sits entirely on the winning side of the premium/mass bifurcation — premium technical brands compound 25–30% at 57–63% gross margins while Nike/VF retrench, releasing share. Sector niche rated Attractive, conditional on Arc'teryx brand heat (Lululemon is the mortality template). Macro is a *multiple problem, not an earnings problem*: reflation with a hawkish paused Fed, 10Y 5.13%/30Y 5.47%, dollar rally threatening to flip the embedded ~200bp FX tailwind into a headwind. Negative skew; macro bear case is $22–24 even on in-line earnings.
- **Geopolitical & Legal: HIGH.** ~95% Asia sourcing (27% China) sits under a new June-2026 Section 301 forced-labour track covering up to 16 countries; ~25–28% of revenue is in politically sensitive, boycott-prone Greater China (the Sept-2025 Tibet fireworks incident drew a ~600m-view backlash and an official probe); an active securities class action; and a dense PFAS/UFLPA/EU Forced Labour compliance calendar through 2027. Q2-26's 390bp margin lift from tariff refunds proves policy — not just brand — moves this P&L.
- **Equity Fundamentals — Value: HOLD.** Narrow-but-widening moat; ROIC inflecting 0.8% → ~12%; FCF conversion >100%; net debt cut $6.2bn → ~$0.45bn. But blended DCF fair value is ~$31 (base $30/bull $42/bear $21), falling to ~$28 at the 11% WACC a 1.97 beta implies — zero margin of safety at $30.24. Buy below $24, sell above $42.
- **Equity Fundamentals — Growth: BUY (high conviction).** Revenue re-accelerating (guide raised 20–22% → 25–26%), 7/7 beat rate with +59% avg surprise, FY26–30E EPS CAGR ~22.6% at 18.4x FY27E (PEG ~1.0), ~4–5% share of a $150–200bn serviceable market with Salomon Softgoods as the next leg. Own caveat: US Arc'teryx search interest collapsed post-April 2026 — growth is being carried by China/DTC.
- **Quantitative Signals: NEUTRAL, tilt negative (−0.6σ).** Bottom-half of the comp set on value, momentum *and* quality (last on ROE and GP/assets); highest beta in peer set; 12-1 momentum −16.2% in an intact downtrend of lower highs. Trailing multiples are stale artifacts (39.8x P/E vs 23.1x FY26E), and with ~1.8 years of history no statistic is robust (alpha t ≈ −1.2). Screens Sell on factor ranks; forward earnings power holds it at Neutral.
- **Financial Risk: MODERATE** (credit LOW / equity HIGH). Survives a −35% revenue shock without external financing (cash $668m ≈ 1.5x net debt; ICR 12.9x; FCF ~breakeven even in the severe case). The real risk is equity-side: 40–47% vol, −37.4% max drawdown, and $5.0bn of goodwill/intangibles (46% of assets) as the impairment tail. Ignore the book-equity Altman Z of 1.81 — market-cap-adjusted Z ≈ 4.2, safe zone.
- **Non-Financial Risk: HIGH.** Zero insider purchases in 12 months against CEO sale of 500k shares (~$17.2m) and the CSO exiting ~78% of direct holdings; ANTA deploying ~$1.8bn into a competing 29% Puma stake while AS trades 28% off its high; controlled-company governance with ANTA nomination rights over 5/11 directors; FPI disclosure regime (no 10-K/10-Q/proxy) limiting related-party monitoring; CEO doubling as interim Salomon/Outdoor head.
- **ESG: AVERAGE / thesis-neutral.** Genuine environmental leadership (SBTi-validated −90% absolute Scope 1–3 targets, 86% renewable electricity, ePE PFAS transition largely pre-incurred) offset by the Tibet values-credibility failure and the China brand-trust concentration — a low-probability, high-severity tail, not a cash-flow drag. Governance merits a small multiple discount.
- **Alternative Data: BULLISH.** Arc'teryx US search interest roughly doubled off its summer trough into November; Salomon search at its best since June (+~40% YoY); arcteryx.com traffic +40% MoM in October — and this is share gain, not sector beta (HOKA searches flat-to-down). Consistent with Q4 tracking ~1–2% above consensus, with the beat more likely in EPS than revenue. Confidence Medium: two data families, and China — the highest-margin region — is a blind spot.
- **Short / Contrarian View: NO EDGE — reject as forensic short.** Earnings quality is clean (negative accruals, DSO improving, no receivables stuffing), short interest only 2.7% of float. The credible bear case is valuation/concentration: strip ~$0.09–0.11 of tariff refunds → FY26 EPS ~$1.20; if China mean-reverts and FY27 lands ~$1.40 at 15x, that's ~$21 (−30%). Defined triggers, not falsifications.

---

**Bull Case**
- **Durable 20%+ compounding at a discount to itself**: 25–26% growth, PEG ~1.0, 18.4x FY27E, estimates rising through a −28% de-rating — sentiment, not fundamentals, has done the damage; the analyst cluster ($42 median) is the re-rating path.
- **Self-reinforcing fundamentals**: margin mix shift (DTC >50% of sales, Arc'teryx DTC +32%), SG&A leverage, ROIC toward mid-teens, net cash, and a $1bn buyback (~5.6% of shares) putting a mechanical bid under the stock into year-end.
- **Alt data inflecting into the catalyst**: US brand demand re-accelerating into Q4 against consensus that models a deceleration (+19% vs +23–32% delivered); a fifth consecutive beat-and-raise on ~23 Feb 2027 breaks the de-rating narrative.

**Bear Case**
- **China is the whole story and the whole risk**: ~25–28% of revenue, ~44% of Arc'teryx sales, ~85–90% of incremental growth — in a market with +0.4% retail sales, nationalist backlash precedent, and a Chinese controlling shareholder with conflicts of interest (Puma stake, related-party distribution).
- **Margin quality is flattered**: 390bps of Q2's 710bps GM gain was non-recurring tariff refunds; 2027–28 consensus EPS implicitly requires continued expansion from ~61% GM — a level that invites both mean-reversion and competition (ON at 62.8% GM is attacking directly).
- **A fair price meets a hostile tape**: zero margin of safety at $30, highest beta in the peer set, negative momentum, insider selling with no offsetting buys, and a rates/FX regime explicitly working against the multiple.

**Key Risks**
1. Greater China deceleration below +25% for two consecutive quarters (the short-desk trigger and the value thesis's axle)
2. Tariff regime escalation (Section 301 forced-labour action) hitting 95% Asia-sourced COGS; refund benefits lapping in H1-27 comps
3. Multiple compression: 22.7x forward at beta ~1.5–2.0 in a 5%+ 10Y world — a shift to 16–18x is a 25% drawdown on unchanged earnings
4. Governance event: ANTA sell-down, related-party expansion, or further insider liquidation
5. Inventory build (+33% YoY, ~232 days) converting to markdowns if sell-through slows; goodwill impairment ($5.0bn) on any Arc'teryx stumble
6. Arc'teryx brand-cycle mortality (the Lululemon template) — sector team's flagged #1 structural risk

**Portfolio Construction Note**

Size this as a **high-beta satellite, not a core holding**: 40–47% annualised vol, beta ~1.5–2.0, and a demonstrated −30%-in-six-weeks drawdown capacity argue for a **starter position of 0.75–1.0% NAV maximum** (half a normal single-name weight), funded from low-beta consumer staples rather than adding to discretionary beta. Do **not** pair with DECK/ONON — correlations of 0.59–0.65 mean no diversification. Execution discipline: hold the starter through the Feb-2027 print; **add toward 1.5% only below ~$26** (near the Value team's $24 buy zone and the September $26.10 low, where the risk/reward finally offers a margin of safety); **trim above ~$40** into the analyst-target cluster. Hard review triggers — any one of: two quarters of China growth <+25%, FY27 gross-margin guidance flat-to-down, inventory days >240 ex-seasonal, confirmed ANTA stake sale, or insider selling resuming post-lockup — move this to Sell regardless of price. The China blind spot in our alternative data and the FPI disclosure gap mean position size must carry the residual uncertainty that research cannot close.

---

*Dissent log: Growth says BUY (PEG 1.0, estimates rising); Value says HOLD (FV ≈ price); Quant says negative-tilt (factor ranks, momentum); Macro says negative skew. The HOLD verdict splits the difference: the growth case is real but the price already pays for it, and the tail risks are concentrated where disclosure is thinnest. Data gaps flagged by the team: peer multiples, Q3-26 segment detail, primary filings (FPI), debt maturity ladder, China alt-data, same-period revision breadth.*

## SECTOR BRIEF — Amer Sports, Inc. (NYSE: AS)
**Sector:** Consumer Cyclical / Leisure — premium technical apparel, outdoor equipment & racquet sports
**Data as of:** Q3 2026 results (reported 17 Nov 2026); market cap $17.6bn, price $30.24, beta 1.97

---

### 1. Sector Overview

AS competes in the ~$175bn global outdoor apparel market (2026E, growing ~5.4% CAGR to ~$239bn by 2032) and the broader ~$400–500bn sporting goods market. The sector is **highly fragmented at the aggregate level** — Nike (~$46bn revenue), adidas, VF Corp ($9.6bn), Lululemon ($11.1bn) and AS ($6.6bn) together hold well under 25% of a global market, implying a low HHI (<500) — but **sharply concentrated within niches**: Arc'teryx in premium technical outerwear, Salomon in trail running and ski, Wilson in racquet sports. The critical structural feature in 2026 is a **bifurcation**: mass athletic is in a tariff-and-destocking trough (Nike revenue +0.2%, operating margin collapsed 336bps to 8.2%; VF −5.1% four-year CAGR), while **premium/technical brands are compounding 25–30%** at 57–63% gross margins. AS sits entirely on the winning side of that split.

### 2. Key Tailwinds

- **Premiumisation and mix shift are visibly pricing through.** AS group gross margin has risen from 49.1% (FY21) to 57.6% (FY25) — +853bps in four years — with FY26 adjusted gross margin guided to ~60.8%. This is not cost-driven; it is Arc'teryx-weighted mix and full-price DTC (Arc'teryx DTC +32% in Q3'26).
- **Greater China premium outdoor remains the sector's best growth market.** China's outdoor sports industry exceeds $422bn with explicit policy support, and premium outdoor is pulling in younger, female and luxury-adjacent consumers. AS grew Greater China revenue 30.4% to $601.6m in Q3'26 *against* a soft Chinese consumer — and its Anta-led ownership gives it distribution no Western peer can replicate.
- **Incumbent retrenchment is releasing share and shelf space.** Nike's restructuring (op. margin 12.3%→8.2%) and VF's contraction have opened wholesale doors and consumer mindshare. AS, DECK and ON are the share takers — the three fastest growers in the table are also the three with the strongest margin trajectory.

### 3. Key Headwinds

- **Tariffs are the number-one industry hurdle and AS is directly exposed.** Section 301 forced-labour tariffs added 12.5% on China and Vietnam-sourced goods from 24 July 2026, on top of existing layers; apparel/footwear sourcing is concentrated in exactly those countries. Tellingly, AS's Q2'26 operating margin got a **390bp one-off lift from net tariff refunds** — proof of the exposure — and FY26 guidance leans on benefits that do not repeat. Industry commentary expects flat-to-negative H1 comps on tariffs.
- **China concentration cuts both ways.** Greater China is now ~$600m/quarter and the fastest-growing region; it is also the region most exposed to stimulus withdrawal, nationalist sentiment toward foreign brands, and geopolitical escalation. Anta's majority stake adds governance and political-sensitivity overhang.
- **"Gorpcore" fashion-cycle risk in the highest-multiple franchise.** Arc'teryx's growth is partly fashion-led, and Lululemon is the cautionary template in this very table: revenue growth decelerated 18.6% → 10.1% → 4.9% and operating margin fell 23.7% → 19.9% in three years. ON Holding (30% growth, 62.8% GM) is also attacking premium footwear directly.

### 4. Peer Comparison

| Columbia (COLM) | Dec-25 | $3,397m | +0.8% | +2.1% | 50.2% (+0.9pp) | 6.0% (−5.3pp) |

*Notes: AS FY26 guidance is +25–26% revenue and adjusted op. margin 14.5–14.7% (GAAP-equivalent ~11.5–12.5%), which would push AS to ~+4pp above peer-median margin. Peer set is hand-built — the sector-aggregate endpoint returned misaligned fiscal periods (company_count 1–3), so no reliable sector blended figure exists. Adidas, Puma and Anta are excluded (non-US filings unavailable). Valuation multiples were not obtainable from the available tooling.*

### 5. Target Company's Competitive Position: **STRONG**

- **Growth:** fastest in the peer set bar ON, at 6–9x the median. Revenue has more than doubled from $3.07bn (FY21) to $6.57bn (FY25), with FY26E ~$8.2–8.3bn — no year below +16%.
- **Margins:** gross margin above peer median and expanding faster than any comparable except ON (+853bps). GAAP operating margin is now exactly at peer median (10.4%) but from a far weaker base (1.4% in FY22) and still ~5–9pp below DECK/LULU, leaving visible self-help runway as DTC mix and SG&A leverage (47.3% of sales in FY25 vs 52.6% in FY22) continue.
- **Balance sheet/cash flow:** the post-IPO deleveraging is the under-appreciated driver — interest expense fell from $401.7m (FY23) to $97.7m (FY25), swinging net income from −$252.7m to +$427.4m, with $1.11bn EBITDA and a $1bn buyback authorised.
- **Caveats:** sub-scale versus Nike ($46bn) at $6.6bn; brand concentration in Arc'teryx for both growth and margin; only ~2.5 years of public reporting (IPO Feb-24 at $13 vs $30.24 now); beta 1.97 means the equity amplifies any sector de-rating.

### 6. Sector Rating: **ATTRACTIVE** (for AS's premium-technical niche) — **NEUTRAL** for mass athletic

The addressable sub-sector offers ~5–7% structural volume growth, genuine pricing power, and a clear share-shift tailwind from wounded incumbents; AS's own guide of 25–26% growth on a $6.6bn base implies years of runway before it meets category growth. The offset is that premium technical looks **late-cycle on margin** — 57–63% gross margins attract entrants (ON is proof), tariffs are a real and rising cost line, and fashion-driven demand can decelerate as violently as Lululemon's did. Rating is Attractive *conditional on* Arc'teryx brand heat persisting; the single largest risk in this thesis is not sector demand but brand-cycle mortality.

**Data gaps:** sector-aggregate financials unavailable (broken periods); no valuation multiples; Adidas/Puma/Anta not covered. Q3'26 segment-level revenue and margin detail was not retrievable (press release timed out); the segment margin structure cited in-text (Technical Apparel ~20% adj. op. margin, Outdoor ~17.5%, Ball & Racquet ~6.9%) is from Q3 2024 disclosure and should be treated as directional.

# Amer Sports, Inc. (NYSE: AS) — Geopolitical & Legal Risk Assessment

*Prepared as of the latest available data (Q3 2026 results reported 17-Nov-2026). Company: Cayman-incorporated (ISIN KYG0260P1028), HQ Helsinki, ~15,400 employees, operations in 40 countries, products sold in 100+, FY2025 revenue $6.6bn. Controlled by the ANTA Sports-led consortium (China).*

## 1. Geographic Risk Map

| Geography | % of FY25 revenue | Key exposures | Risk level |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Americas** (US-dominant) | ~36% | Section 301 / Section 232 tariffs on Asian-sourced goods; US securities litigation; consumer cyclicality | **Medium** |
| **Greater China** | ~25–28% (≈$1.86bn, +43% YoY) | Nationalist/consumer backlash, regulatory & permitting scrutiny, macro slowdown, ANTA related-party dependence | **High** |
| **EMEA** | ~29% | EU PFAS (REACH PFHxA, eff. 10-Oct-2026), EU Forced Labour Regulation & CSDDD, FX | **Low–Medium** |
| **Asia Pacific ex-China** | ~10% | Sourcing/transit hub (Vietnam, etc.) exposed to new Section 301 actions | **Medium** |
| **Sourcing footprint (cost, not revenue)** | — | ~27% Greater China, ~68% elsewhere APAC (~95% Asia) | **High** |

Sources: Amer Sports annual report/IR ("Americas 36%, EMEA 29%, Greater China 25%, APAC 10%"); Jing Daily (Greater China $1.86bn, +43.4%); Amer Sports supply-chain transparency page ("Greater China 27%, other Asia Pacific 68%"); Q2-26 release ("operations in 40 countries, products sold in 100+").

## 2. Top 3 Geopolitical Risks

**1) Tariff-regime volatility and the new Section 301 forced-labour action — Probability: High / Impact: Medium-High**
The Supreme Court's **20-Feb-2026** decision invalidating IEEPA tariffs (affirming *V.O.S. Selections*) forced a rescission of those duties and opened refund claims; Amer booked a **$50.1m net tariff refund benefit** and **390bps of gross-margin benefit in Q2-26** — a single-quarter swing that demonstrates how tariff policy, not brand performance, can move reported margins. Guidance explicitly *assumes the most recently announced Section 301 rates remain in place*. On **2-Jun-2026** USTR announced new Section 301 proposals arising from a forced-labour investigation covering as many as 16 countries including China (potentially textiles/apparel) — directly aimed at Amer's sourcing base (~95% Asia). With ~95% of COGS sourced in Asia and ~36% of revenue in the Americas, a renewed escalation (or country-specific action on Vietnam) is the most probable adverse policy event. Mitigant: pricing power at Arc'teryx/Salomon and demonstrated ability to pass through (GM still 60.5–61.0% guided for FY26).

**2) China concentration + political/nationalist risk — Probability: Medium / Impact: High**
Greater China is ~25–28% of revenue and the fastest-growing region (group FY26 growth guided ~24%, China compounding at 40%+), making Arc'teryx's China franchise the single largest driver of the equity story. The **Sept-2025 Arc'teryx "Rising" fireworks display in Tibet** triggered a ~600m-view boycott, an official Chinese investigation and the dismissal of four local officials — a live demonstration that a single marketing decision can convert into a state-adjacent and consumer-driven revenue shock. Additional layers: (i) **ANTA Sports indirectly holds ~53–58%** of Amer (with FountainVest, Anamered/Tencent), so China policy and ANTA's own Xinjiang-cotton positioning (Nikkei: the cotton controversy has divided the group) transmit to Amer; (ii) any future US action against Chinese-controlled US-listed issuers (HFCAA-style disclosure/audit or outbound-investment rules) is a tail risk to the listing and index inclusion; (iii) a March-2026 follow-on of 20.6m shares at $36.40 vs. a current ~$30 share price signals that supply overhang/liquidity events around the sponsor stake remain a recurring feature.

**3) US–China strategic rupture (Taiwan, export controls, summit-level diplomacy) — Probability: Medium / Impact: High**
Amer sits precisely at the intersection — American/European brands, Asian manufacturing, Chinese ownership and Chinese growth. The November-2026 Trump–Xi–Putin summit and ongoing Commerce Department export-control tightening (WSJ, 17-Nov-2026) show the relationship remains transactional and headline-driven. A deterioration would hit all three legs simultaneously: Chinese consumer sentiment toward Western premium brands, tariff treatment of Asian sourcing, and the valuation of a China-owned US-listed equity.

## 3. Legal & Regulatory Highlights

- **Securities class action (active).** Filed after the Sept-2025 Tibet incident; firm investigations (Pomerantz, Levi & Korsinsky) allege materially misleading statements/disclosures; AS fell >5% on 22-Sep-2025. Amer already excludes "expenses related to certain legal proceedings" from adjusted EPS — i.e., litigation is recurring and material enough to be a standing adjustment. Dismissal/settlement outcome not confirmed in available sources (**gap**).
- **Employment litigation:** *EEOC v. Amer Sports Winter & Outdoor Co.* — $350,000 settlement and consent decree entered in D. Colo. on **6-Mar-2026** (age discrimination/retaliation). Small dollar value; relevant as a pattern of US employment-process exposure.
- **Product/PFAS regulation (under-appreciated, near-term):** EU REACH restriction on **PFHxA applies to apparel from 10-Oct-2026** (25ppb); California **AB 1817** PFAS ban in effect since 1-Jan-2025 (severe-wet-conditions outerwear exempt until 1-Jan-2028) plus New York. This hits the highest-margin waterproof/technical outerwear (Arc'teryx, Salomon) — a materials-reformulation cost and compliance-failure risk.
- **Supply-chain due diligence:** US **UFLPA** (Xinjiang) import detentions, **EU Forced Labour Regulation** (applicable 2027) and CSDDD create traceability obligations across the 27% China sourcing base; brands in this peer set have already been named in NGO/reporting lists alongside Amer.
- **Data privacy/consumer:** DTC reached ~49% of revenue in 2025 → GDPR, China PIPL, CCPA, plus advertising/marketing claims scrutiny (greenwashing and "performance" claims are an active regulatory theme in the EU).
- **IP:** Counterfeiting of Arc'teryx/Salomon in China is an ongoing brand-equity and enforcement cost; no material disclosed IP verdict.
- **Governance:** Controlled-company status (ANTA consortium) limits minority influence; related-party distribution in Greater China and sponsor sell-downs are the key conflict vectors.

## 4. Compliance Red Flags

1. **Supply-chain traceability (elevated):** ~27% China sourcing with UFLPA/EU FLR exposure and a publicly documented internal split over Xinjiang cotton — detention or forced-labour findings would be a direct revenue and reputational hit.
2. **Litigation-adjusted earnings:** recurring "certain legal proceedings" add-backs mean adjusted EPS quality warrants scrutiny.
3. **China growth + state-adjacent sensitivity:** the Tibet episode shows non-financial risk converting to revenue risk quickly; ESG/permitting failures in China are a live compliance channel.
4. No evidence of sanctions (OFAC/Russia), FCPA/DOJ or AML exposure identified — consumer branded goods, limited high-risk-jurisdiction footprint beyond China sourcing.

## 5. Overall Geopolitical/Legal Risk Rating: **HIGH**

Rationale: ~95% of sourcing concentrated in Asia (27% China) with an active new Section 301 forced-labour track; ~25–28% of revenue in a politically sensitive, boycott-prone Greater China market that is also the primary growth engine; a Chinese state-linked controlling shareholder; an active securities class action; and a dense 2026–27 regulatory calendar (PFAS, EU Forced Labour Regulation, CSDDD). Offsets: no sanctions exposure, strong pricing power (60.5–61.0% guided gross margin), demonstrated tariff pass-through, and a geographically diversified revenue base (Americas 36% / EMEA 29%). This is a *high* but not *very high* rating — the risks are policy-conjunctural rather than structural (no nationalisation, currency-control or expropriation exposure, and no direct Russia/OFAC nexus).

**Gaps:** No 10-K/10-Q text was retrievable through the filing tool (only Form 4 metadata returned), so exact legal-proceedings language, committed tariff dollar exposure and the current ANTA ownership percentage could not be confirmed from primary filings; figures above rely on company releases, IR pages and press reporting.

# Macroeconomic Assessment — Amer Sports, Inc. (NYSE: AS)
**As of 18 November 2026 | Price $30.24 | Mkt cap $17.6B | Beta 1.97 | Sector: Consumer Cyclical / Leisure**

---

## 1. Macro Environment Summary — **Transitional, risk-off tilt**
